With a regionally varying cost of CO , the MFSP for the 2 membrane system ranges from $9.5 to $37.3 per GGE. The results in Figure 3-33 were compared with the MFSP for the sparging scenario to show the difference in costs between the two carbon delivery systems (Figure 3-34). This comparison indicates an overall higher MFSP when installing and operating the membrane system with a constant cost of CO . Costs increase by $1.6 to $5.9 per GGE 2 depending on location within the US due to higher capital and operational costs for membranes, tanks, and circulation systems as well as the inability of the membrane system to meet the total carbon demand because of insufficient DiC molarity exiting the membrane combined with pond volume limitations. However, when applying a varying cost of CO , the membrane system shows favorable economics compared to 2 the sparging system, lowering the MFSP by up to $2.5 per GGE in some locations. Regional grid emissions obtained from eGRID (US EPA 2020) and Summers et al. (2021) were used to generate spatio-temporal LCA results for algae cultivation across the US with each of the evaluated carbon delivery systems (Figures 3-35 and 3-36). The results shown in Figures 3-35 suggest higher overall greenhouse gas emissions when using the enzymatic membrane system (from -0.7 to 1.5 kg CO -eq/kg AFDW) compared to traditional gas sparging (from - 2 1.3 to 0.9 kg CO -eq/kg AFDW). The higher emissions can be attributed to 2 insufficient DiC concentration exiting the membrane and the need for supplemental sodium bicarbonate addition to the ponds. In addition to determining the GWP for algae cultivation, the well-to-wheels GWP was determined for algal cultivation (with both sparging and the membrane) and fuel conversion via HTL (Figure 3-8). The results in Figure 3-36 suggest a well-to-wheels GWP ranging from 71.7 to 223.7 g CO -eq per MJ fuel for when using the membrane system and a GWP ranging 2 from 26.1 to 180.5 g CO -eq per MJ fuel when using traditional gas sparging. From 2 the results, there are no locations throughout the US in which the well-to-wheels GWP for the membrane system is below the renewable fuels standard for renewable diesel (~45 g CO -eq/MJ fuel); however, however, several locations along the West 2 Coast and in the southern US satisfy the renewable fuels standard when using gas sparging. Regional differences are due to varying productivity as well as varying greenhouse gas intensity for the different grid regions.
